newsitem.title: UK: British retailers wary of Social Chapter.
newsitem.headline: British retailers wary of Social Chapter.

text.p: A leading British retailers group voiced its concern on Monday about the European Union's Social Chapter but said it was not against its objectives.

"As an industry we are concerned about some of the implications of the Social Chapter and prospective minimum wage," Mark Souhami, chairman of the British Retail Consortium told the BRC's annual dinner.
He said the BRC did not object to the principles of the Social Chapter, which guarantees minimum rights for workers.
"What we resist is the idea that there should be a single universal set of conditions covering all types of employment."
He said inflexible rules like that suggested only fixed- hours, full-time jobs were worthwhile. "They are not."
The opposition Labour Party has said it would sign up for the Social Chapter and introduce a minimum wage if it were to take power after elections due by May.
The ruling Conservatives, lagging badly in the polls, reject the idea of a minimum wage and have refused to sign the EU's Social Chapter.

Souhami said plans for a single European currency were also of crucial importance to retailers. "Whatever one's views about the desirability of a single currency, there is no doubt that a very great burden of implementation will fall upon retailers."
He said present EU proposals could cost European retailers some 21.5 billion pounds and called for implementation plans to be simplified to avoid confusing customers.
Both the Conservative and Labour parties have officially kept their options open over joining European economic and monetary union at its proposed start date of January 1, 1999.
